answer.label: Not Dr. Seuss — actually Anita Merina
answer.authorDates: National Education Association writer · author of the 1997 Read Across America verse
answer.sourceLine: The lines come from a short poem written by Anita Merina, a staff member of the National Education Association, around 1997 for the NEA’s “Read Across America” campaign. Its earliest documented printing was a March 1998 guest column in The Augusta Chronicle, where it was correctly credited to Merina. Dr. Seuss (Theodor Seuss Geisel) died in 1991 and could not have written it; the verse only sounds like him because the campaign it promoted was built around his birthday and legacy, per Quote Investigator ↗.

source.excerpt: It’s never too cold, too wet or too hot / To pick up a book, and share what you’ve got / You’re never too old, too wacky, too wild / To pick up a book, and read to a child
trail: Traced to Anita Merina. Quote Investigator ↗ found the verse was composed by NEA staffer Anita Merina around 1997, with its earliest printing in The Augusta Chronicle in March 1998.
Seuss died in 1991. Theodor Seuss Geisel died six years before the poem was written, so the popular Dr. Seuss credit is chronologically impossible per Quote Investigator ↗.
Correctly credited elsewhere. Goodreads catalogs the same lines under Anita Merina’s name ↗, even as most quote sites still tag it “Dr. Seuss.”

author.name: Anita Merina
author.heading: About Anita Merina
author.metaLine: National Education Association writer · author of the 1997 Read Across America reading verse
author.bio: Anita Merina was a communications staff member at the National Education Association (NEA), which created its “Read Across America” literacy campaign in 1997 and held the first Read Across America Day on March 2, 1998 — the birthday of Theodor Seuss Geisel. Around that time she wrote the short rhyming verse whose couplet, “You’re never too old, too wacky, too wild, to pick up a book and read to a child,” became widely quoted. Because the campaign celebrated Dr. Seuss, her Seuss-flavored lines were soon misattributed to him.

misattribution.heading: How Dr. Seuss got the credit
misattribution.intro: This is a classic case of a Seuss-flavored rhyme getting pinned on Dr. Seuss himself. The verse promotes a campaign named for him, so the leap to crediting him was easy — and wrong.

items.scope: The couplet “You’re never too old, too wacky, too wild, to pick up a book and read to a child”
items.why: Endlessly reproduced under his name by quote sites, greeting cards and library posters — but Geisel died in 1991, and the poem was not written until around 1997, per Quote Investigator ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: The real author is Anita Merina of the National Education Association, who wrote the verse around 1997 for “Read Across America”; it first appeared in print in March 1998, as documented by Quote Investigator ↗.

context.heading: A campaign line, not a storybook line
lead: The NEA created “Read Across America” in 1997 and held the first Read Across America Day on March 2, 1998 — Dr. Seuss’s birthday — as a national push to get adults reading aloud to kids. Anita Merina’s cheerful, Seuss-cadenced verse was written to rally people to that cause.

Because the whole event orbited Dr. Seuss, the rhyme was quickly absorbed into “things Dr. Seuss said,” even though it postdates his death by roughly six years. The sentiment is squarely in the spirit of his legacy; the exact words are Merina’s.
context.pull: It sounds like Seuss because it was written to celebrate Seuss — not by him.
